The diagram below shows how rainwater is collected, stored and reused in a house.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: How rainwater is collected and reused in a house
steps: Rain falls onto the roof and runs into gutters
Gutters carry the water into a downpipe
Leaves and debris are removed by a leaf screen
Filtered water flows into an underground storage tank
Sediment settles at the bottom of the tank
A pump draws water from the tank when it is needed
Water is pumped to the toilets and the washing machine
Excess water leaves the tank through an overflow pipe

body:
The diagram below shows how a tidal barrage generates electricity from the rise and fall of the sea.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: How a tidal barrage generates electricity
steps: Seawater flows into the basin through sluice gates on the incoming tide
The sluice gates close once the basin is full at high tide
Water is held in the basin while the sea level outside falls
When the difference in level is large enough, the turbine gates open
Water rushes out of the basin through the turbines
The turbines drive generators that produce electricity
Electricity is sent to the national grid through underground cables
At low demand, turbines can run in reverse to pump water into the basin
Sediment settles on the basin floor and is removed by dredging
Dredged material is taken ashore and used in construction
Sensors send faults back to maintenance before the cycle restarts

body:
The maps below show a river valley in 1990 and in 2024, after a dam and a reservoir were built across it.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: A river valley before and after a dam and reservoir were built

features: A small village lies on the north bank of the river
A wooden bridge crosses the river next to the village
Farmland covers the flat land on the south side of the valley
A main road runs along the east side of the valley
A railway line crosses the valley in the west
A water mill stands beside the river in the south-west corner
A school is on the edge of the village, near the main road
A petrol station sits at the road junction in the middle of the valley
Two fishing huts are on the river bank to the east
Forest covers the hills to the north of the village
The village has been moved to the hillside in the north-east corner
The wooden bridge next to the old village site has been removed
A concrete dam stretches across the narrowest point of the valley in the west
A large reservoir fills the valley behind the dam in the centre
The water mill has been converted into a visitor centre beside the dam
The railway line has been rerouted along the eastern edge of the reservoir
A small power station stands at the foot of the dam on the south side
The main road now runs across the top of the dam
The school has been rebuilt next to the new village
The fishing huts have been removed from the river bank
Forest on the hills to the north is still unchanged

body:

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: A farm site before and after its conversion into a solar farm

features: A farmhouse stands in the north-west corner next to the lane
A large orchard covers the east side of the site
Four arable fields lie between the lane and the pond
A wooden barn stands in the centre of the site
A pond lies in the south-west corner
A hedge runs along the southern boundary
A gravel lane runs along the western boundary to the farmhouse

after.label: Planned
features: Rows of solar panels cover the four fields between the lane and the pond
The farmhouse remains in the north-west corner next to the lane, unchanged
The orchard on the east side is kept, with footpaths running through it
The barn in the centre will be converted into a visitor centre with a cafe
A car park will be built next to the lane near the entrance
The pond in the south-west corner will be enlarged
A bird hide is planned on the bank of the enlarged pond
The hedge along the southern boundary is kept
